entry: 5.1 Handwritten lecture material and the English donor
statement: G.'s uniqueness conjecture for admissible integral PD de Rham theories (cote 136, scans 111-121, the lecture material of 095-141): a generalized theory is a bigraded differential PD algebra functor with augmentation, admissible when the augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism after τ_∞ ("cohomologie de De Rham associée", 111-113; "l'augmentation est un quasi-iso", 117); "On aimerait prouver un th. d'unicité" (119), first step "on oublie d'abord la structure p.d." (119); on 121 every allowed morphism is already a τ_∞ quasi-isomorphism ("les hom. … sont déjà des quasi-iso"), and the localized groupoid of admissible theories should be "connexe et simplement connexe ?", through "Conj.? a)" (two admissible theories receive maps from a third) and an equalization condition ("qui égalise"), with "calcul de fractions à droite ???" in the margin. Prove or refute connectedness and simple connectedness, with and without the PD structure. The simple-connectedness half is to be compared with G.'s later classification of the endomorphisms and automorphisms of his PD de Rham functor (#243: a scalar part and a pro-unipotent kernel), and the two automorphism groups of 104-106 ("deux groupes, que nous nous proposons de déterminer") with the same classification. entry: N39 — The \(D^+\) full-faithfulness claim requires a derived unit
statement: G.'s weight localization and its multiplication (cote 136, scans 244-281: "Généralités sur modules gradués sur certains anneaux gradués" (244), "n'est pas une catégorie à lim filtrantes exactes" (254), "bijectif?" (257), full faithfulness on D⁺(C) "pl. fid." and "compatible avec multiplication" (273), "Th. Le foncteur τ_N i_* est pl. fid." (279)). Setting: S = Γ_k(T) = k{T}, M_0 the nonnegative graded S-modules, i(M) = M ⊗_k S. Settled in our notes: finite-tail full faithfulness (g1031; Michel Hua's project's finding, credit to his project), an exact left adjoint L of i (g1041), the failure of G.'s literal negligible classes (g1034, g1035), and, in a repaired setting (the Gabriel quotient Q by the localizing Serre closure of the bounded-above modules), the derived reconstruction RR Q i(M) ≅ i(M) (g1080), which gives the linear "pl. fid." on D⁺. Open, and the item: "compatible avec multiplication" (273). Construct, naturally in the simplicial set X, a multiplicative structure on the weight-localized PD de Rham complex (at least a ring object in D(k)) that recovers the cup product, or prove that none exists. Starting facts: the naive product [p]_a ⊗ [q]_b ↦ [p ⊗ q]_{a+b} does not descend through L, since C(a+b+m, a+b) ≠ C(a+m, a), and along the cofinal weights a = b = ℓ^r − 1 the factor C(2ℓ^r − 2, ℓ^r − 1) has ℓ-adic valuation r (Kummer) (the gap reader's computation, unchecked); integer combinations of weighted products recover the cup product on cohomology (g1082: 6·C(4,2) − C(7,3) = 1; g1081 for the conditional route); no strict integral PD algebra can carry the cup product (g1019, CP²). entry: 120-CJ1 — Conjecture — The marginal restriction on elementary models
statement: G.'s converse for elementary U (cote 149, scan 120, ms. p. 60: "A t-on une réciproque ? regarder !", and the margin "Ça devrait être le cas pour U 'élémentaire'" with the underlined types (0,0) and (0,1), whose connecting words are uncertain). Let U be an elementary (anabelian) scheme over a field K of characteristic 0 with function field L, and V a valuation of L trivial on K. Prove or refute: if the inertia group I_V maps trivially into E_U^{L̄} (the arithmetic fundamental group, 149/117), then V has a centre on U. Known in the notes: the forward implication, and the failure for U = A¹ (type (0,1), g1277). The gap reader's check (unchecked): for curves, a valuation without centre on U is centred at a cusp, whose inertia is trivial in π_1 only for type (0,1), so the curve case holds for every other type; the content is in dimension ≥ 2 and for non-divisorial valuations (centres at normal-crossing boundary points: injectivity of the local Ẑ(1)^r into π_1(U), e.g. for M_{0,n}). G. recovers E_U from G_L by killing the inertia of the valuations centred on U (149/121, g1278); the item says that no other inertia dies. The object: a projective bundle over S with marked pseudo-reflections T_i(v) = v + φ_i(v)a_i (λ_i = 1 + μ_i units), an admissible pinned flag whose orbit gives the realization, a centre and a distinguished hyperplane; on the finite-centre chart (ρ invertible, 073-074) a rank-(n+1) module with φ_i(a_i) = λ_i − 1, predecessor pairings 1 and successor pairings β_i.
